title: Usage signals and capacity playbook - Cascade Systems QBR
next_steps: Redwood to share revised reserved pricing scenarios and burst playbook
Customer to provide 2 weeks of request traces and golden prompt set
Schedule pilot stress run on Dedicated: week of Dec 6
action_items: Maya: Share dedicated vs hosted pricing spreadsheet by 2027-11-24
Nora: Export 14 days of p95/p99 traces and send to Redwood (anonymized) by 2027-11-26
Liam: Prepare pilot run checklist + runbook by 2027-11-30
Elena: Confirm internal pilot stakeholders and success metrics by 2027-11-25
transcript: Header: 2027-11-21 16:00 UTC | Duration: 54m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Rajiv Patel (Cascade VP Eng), Nora Kim (SRE), Elena Rossi (Product)
Summary: QBR-style health check focused on unusual usage signals in last quarter, cost variance, latency spikes during batch windows, and alignment on a Dedicated pilot and roadmap for H1 2028.
Topics: usage trends, cost spikes, latency incidents, dedicated pilot scoping, security and compliance check, next steps and runbook.
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we' ll try to keep to 45ish minutes then leave time for q's. quick agenda—usage signals, costs, perf incidents, and pilot plan for dedicated capacity.
[00:24] Rajiv: yeah thanks, the team sent over the dashboard — just a heads up we saw a pattern of mid-day p99 jumps last week while daily cost also crept up unexpectedly.
[00:40] Nora: mm hm, it's mostly the inference path for our conversational assistant, the traffic is pretty bursty, and we had a couple of latency escalations around 11am-1pm PST which impacted SLAs.
[01:05] Liam: ok can you confirm whether those spikes were correlated with longer context lengths or sudden payload size changes? sometimes the kv cache warm up causes p99 tails.

[01:27] Nora: we think both — a new campaign increased average token lengths and also we rolled a prompt set that uses additional tool calls. the KV cache — sometimes i see log entries for cache misses but they were labeled KV cash in the old log, so could be noise.

[01:54] Maya: (laughs) yes KV cash — classic transcription artifact — but the point stands. we looked at your billing export and there was a step function increase in token units on Nov 3rd, then sustained higher baseline.
[02:19] Rajiv: that aligns — we shipped an A/B test with richer context on Nov 2. the product team expected some cost but not this magnitude. curious if batching or prefix caching could help.

[02:40] Liam: definitely. we recommended a two-pronged approach: 1) short-term—intelligent batching + request shaping on the client side, 2) mid-term—pilot Dedicated with reserved capacity and prefix/KV caching enabled at the runtime layer.
[03:05] Elena: how much lift is the client-side change? we have a small infra squad but they're stretched. is this something Redwood can help wire up in the pilot?
[03:22] Maya: yes we can assist — our solutions engineering team can provide templates for batching middleware and sample wrappers for common SDKs. for the pilot we can also run integration sessions.
[03:40] Rajiv: ok good. on cost, can you walk through the reserved pricing scenarios again? the spreadsheet we have is a bit hard to map to our weird traffic curves.

[03:58] Liam: sure — there are three flavors: hosted pay-as-you-go, committed Dedicated (monthly commit with burst), and a hybrid where routing steers non-critical requests to cheaper model variants. committed Dedicated reduces unit cost by about 30-45% depending on quantization and burst contract.
[04:26] Nora: is the 30-45% estimate based on our workload profile or on general averages? we mainly care about tail latency and cache warm starts.

[04:40] Liam: it's based on similar mid-market customers with a mix of chat and completion traffic. we'll refine once we have your traces — the quantization profile and sequence length distribution matter a lot.

[04:58] Maya: quick security note — you asked about private keys and audit logs last quarter. Dedicated supports KMS integration and we can push audit logs to your SIEM; for Private deployments we support HSM options as well.
[05:18] Rajiv: good, compliance is on the roadmap. SOC 2 evidence and retention windows are important — we need to know what logs Redwood retains and for how long.
[05:30] Maya: we'll share the security pack again; it includes retention defaults, SSO/SAML flow, RBAC capabilities, and a sample audit log export. i'll attach it to the follow-up.
[06:02] Elena: about the Dedicated pilot — what does success look like? we want cost per 1k tokens to drop, p99 latency under 750ms for 90% of windows, and no error rate regression.
[06:20] Liam: sounds reasonable. operational success criteria: sustained p95/p99 improvements during peak windows, stable throughput at committed QPS, and zero data exfil/privacy issues in logs.
[06:40] Nora: one constraint — we cannot move sensitive logs outside the VPC. will the Dedicated pilot allow the inference VPC peering or must data flow through Redwood control plane?

[06:58] Maya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; the control plane still orchestrates but can be configured for minimal surface area. for full on-prem Private we can discuss later if needed.
[07:18] Rajiv: i want to call out an incident on Nov 9 where a config rollout increased concurrency aggressively and caused a cascading queue — do you have suggestions for guardrails?

[07:36] Liam: yes, we recommend canary rollouts with automatic throttling and a fallback variant. Redwood's rollout engine can do percentage-based canaries and automatic failover to a cheaper smaller model when latency spikes.
[07:58] Rajiv: is that automatic failover available on Hosted or only Dedicated? we prefer hosted but want resilience.
[08:12] Liam: hosted has the same logical features; the difference is that Dedicated gives you reserved headroom and more predictable performance under committed QPS.

[08:28] Maya: practical ask — please send us two weeks of request traces with headers, anonymized; that lets us simulate your specific token lengths and sequence distributions and produce a recommend config.
[08:45] Nora: we'll do that. anything specific about formatting? we have JSON lines from our proxy logs.
[08:55] Liam: JSON lines are perfect; include timestamps and response times, omit PII. we'll take it and run a small perf replay to estimate cost/reserve sizing.
[09:12] Elena: timeframe for the pilot? we're thinking end of year or early Jan; can Redwood support a 2-week pilot with stress runs and a handoff to our infra team?
[09:28] Maya: yes — we're suggesting a pilot week of config + integration, then a focused stress run week. target window: Dec 6 pilot start, finishing Dec 20 with a runbook handoff.
[09:48] Rajiv: ok Dec 6 sounds doable. what about monitoring — can the Redwood console emit metrics to our prometheus stack or do we have to use the Redwood dashboard?
[10:02] Liam: we export metrics via pushgateway or a metrics endpoint; we can also provide tracing hooks and per-route token breakdowns. many customers run dual dashboards during pilots.
[10:20] Nora: we want tracing to tie token cost back to feature flags — then finance can map cost to product experiments.
[10:30] Maya: yep that's a common ask. we'll include an example mapping in the pilot docs.
[10:45] Rajiv: competitor question — we've had internal talks about Anthropic's offerings and OpenAI; any notable tradeoffs we should be aware of as we decide on Dedicated vs staying hosted?

[10:58] Liam: high-level: Anthropic sometimes has strong safety defaults but cost/latency depends on region, OpenAI has a broad model catalog and scale. Redwood differentiates on predictable economics and the routing/fallback story for production stability.
[11:20] Elena: can you quantify expected unit cost delta if we move to Dedicated with 6 month commit? rough numbers to share with finance.

[11:32] Liam: we'll put together scenarios tied to your trace after we get the traces; rough ballpark is 30% saving on token unit cost with a 6-12 month commit, plus lower cold-start costs due to caching.
[11:50] Nora: also want to measure tail latency improvements — is there a way to simulate our worst-case patterns during the pilot? the replay idea sounds good.
[12:06] Maya: we'll run a replay harness in our staging with your anonymized traces. we'll surface p50/p95/p99 and cost delta with batching on and off.
[12:22] Rajiv: on guardrails and runbooks — can you share a template for rollback/playbook actions? the Nov 9 incident showed we need faster kill-switches.

[12:36] Liam: yes, included in the pilot pack: automated throttles, model variant fallback, circuit breakers tied to error rate and latency thresholds, and a manual kill switch controlled via console and API.
[12:55] Elena: perfect. any gotchas we should know before Dec 6? infra, quotas, or firewall rules?
[13:10] Maya: ensure outbound egress to Redwood endpoints for the pilot, open the required ports listed in the onboarding doc, and if you do VPC peering have the right CIDR ranges ready.
[13:28] Nora: we'll coordinate with infra. last question — will the pilot cost be billable? Finance needs to know.
[13:38] Maya: pilot technical work is included; if you use production tokens beyond test quotas there will be normal usage billing. we'll surface an estimate before kickoff.
[13:55] Rajiv: ok sounds good. let's recap next steps then.

[14:05] Maya: recap: Redwood to share updated pricing scenarios + security pack (Maya) by Nov 24; Cascade to send 14-day traces (Nora) by Nov 26; Redwood to prepare pilot runbook and run replay (Liam) by Nov 30; Elena to confirm pilot stakeholders and success metrics by Nov 25.
[14:30] Nora: noted. any final questions?
[14:35] Rajiv: no, thanks everyone. appreciate the practical plan — excited to see if Dedicated reduces our cost tail while keeping latency solid.
[14:49] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the attachments and calendar invites for the pilot prep sessions. talk soon.
End of meeting
